name: Aluminum 6061-T6
notes: Highly machinable, excellent corrosion resistance. Chips tend to weld to the tool edge under heat; use sharp polished cutting flutes and high flood coolant or MQL.

name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5)
notes: Aerospace workhorse. Very poor thermal conductivity; heat remains concentrated on the cutting edge. Work-hardens instantly; require positive cutting geometry and rigid setup.

name: Stainless Steel 304
notes: Austeritic stainless steel. Extremely gummy and prone to work-hardening. Do not dwell or allow tool rubbing. Use cobalt HSS or high performance coated carbide.

name: Alloy Steel 4140 (Annealed)
notes: Chromium-molybdenum medium carbon steel. Hardens to high strength when heat treated. Fairly easy to machine in its annealed state with predictable chip control.

name: Gray Cast Iron Class 25
notes: Brittle material. Generates powdery, abrasive chips. Can be dry machined safely; ensure high dust vacuuming. Extremely stable with low residual stresses.

name: PEEK 30% Glass Filled
notes: High performance polymer. Glass fibers are extremely abrasive and cause rapid tool edge rounding. Use diamond-coated tooling for optimum service life.
